s: Bei mir auf der Arbeit sind fast alle krank. Überall hört man nur hatschi hier, hatschi da.
At my work, almost everybody’s ill. All you hear is achoo here, achoo there.
bless you; gesundheit (used a response to someone’s sneezing, also sometimes one’s own)
Hatten (a municipality of Oldenburg district, Lower Saxony, Germany)

a hat trick; a player’s scoring three goals in one match; as distinct from English usage, the goals are often required to be consecutive, i.e. with no other player of either team scoring in between (see below)
Ich komm' aus Hamburg, du Spast, ich fick' dein Hurenviertel / Sag' den Hatern, ich hol' mir die zweite Uhr in Kürze
to walk in a clumsy, sluggish and rather slow manner; to plod
to walk a long exhausting distance
hatschen.et: Unclear. Middle High German hakezen (“to limp”) and Arabic حَجّ (ḥajj, “pilgrimage”) have been proposed as possible origins.

s: woulda, coulda, shoulda; used to dismiss suggestions about hypothetical courses of action to have taken in the past, focusing on present issues instead
Ja, Herr Lorig, hätte, hätte, hätte Fahrradkette—natürlich hätte das technische Wahlkampf-Management der SPD dies machen sollen. Nun ist auch gut.
Well, Mr. Lorig, woulda coulda shoulda—of course the technical campaign management of the SPD should have done that. Let's move on now.
hätte, hätte, Fahrradkette.et: Literally, “would have, would have, bicycle chain”, mockingly echoing the subjunctive hätte, with Fahrradkette as a nonsensical term added purely for the rhyme while matching the meter. Likely coined in the TV comedy Stromberg in 2007, further popularized in 2…

s: poorly conceived, half-baked (of ideas, plans, etc.)
hatschert.et: Borrowed from Bavarian hatschert. Compare hatschen.

s: a town and municipality of Ennepe-Ruhr-Kreis district, North Rhine-Westphalia
